claims.text: Stepwise aging that forms nanoscale coherent precipitates will improve both room-temperature tensile strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy contains dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The internal lamellar boundaries are typically incoherent or weakly bonded.
Internal lamellar boundaries act as microcrack-initiation sites during tensile deformation.
A two-step post-solidification heat treatment can induce coherent nanoprecipitates.
The induced nanoprecipitates will form along the lamellar interfaces.
A related refractory high-entropy alloy develops δ-lamellae and γ″ precipitates through stepwise processing.
Coherent interfacial precipitates reduce stress concentrations at lamellar boundaries.
The precipitates facilitate homogeneous dislocation motion across lamellar boundaries through a combination of dislocation shearing and pinning.
Modification of the interfaces by coherent precipitates mitigates premature microcrack initiation.
The precipitates contribute to precipitation strengthening.
The treatment will increase ultimate tensile strength by approximately 1 GPa relative to the unmodified lamellar baseline.
The treatment will improve tensile elongation relative to the unmodified lamellar baseline.
The treated alloy will exhibit fewer internally initiated cracks under room-temperature loading.
The related refractory alloy reached an ultimate tensile strength of 2.15 GPa and tensile ductility of 15% at ambient temperature.
In the related refractory alloy, yield strength increased from about 600 MPa in the as-cast condition to about 1.4 GPa after δ-lamella precipitation and 2.0 GPa after γ″-particle precipitation.
The beneficial effect requires a composition capable of forming coherent precipitates.
Excessive aging temperature or duration may produce coarse, incoherent precipitates.
Coarse, incoherent precipitates will not enhance ductility.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies aging in two steps, but the conditions describe only one intermediate-temperature aging stage followed by tensile testing; the second aging step is not defined.
